chunks: Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isam al-Kulayni (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad, known as Bil'an, said: Abu Hamid 'Imran ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim narrated from al-Hasan ibn al-Qasim al-Raqam, from al-Qasim ibn Muslim, from his brother 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Muslim, who said: I asked al-Rida 'Ali ibn Musa (peace be upon them) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
"They forgot Allah, so He forgot them."

He (AS) said: Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, does not forget nor make a mistake. Rather, the created, transient being forgets and makes a mistake. Do you not hear Him, the Mighty and High, saying: "And your Lord is not forgetful"? He rewards the one who forgets Him and forgets the meeting of his Day by making them forget themselves, as the Mighty and High says: "And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He made them forget themselves; those are the defiantly disobedient." And His saying, the Mighty and High: "So today We will forget them as they forgot the meeting of their Day," meaning: We will leave them as they left the preparation for the meeting of their Day. The Compiler of this book said (may Allah be pleased with him): His saying "We will leave them" means: We will not grant them the reward of those who hoped for the meeting of their Day, because "leaving" (attrak) is not proper for Allah, the Mighty and High. As for the saying of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And leave them in darkness so they do not see," it means: He did not hasten punishment upon them and gave them respite so they might repent.
Chapter: The Commentary of the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: "And the whole earth will be in His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be rolled up in His right hand."

key_terms.الِاتْرَاكَ: leaving or abandoning (in a divine context)
key_terms.لِقَاءَ يَوْمِهِ: the meeting of his Day (of Judgment)
key_terms.يَسْهَوُ: to make a mistake or be heedless

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah says 'He forgot them' in the Quran?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies that divine 'forgetting' (nasa) is not literal ignorance but a consequential withdrawal of reward or delay of punishment, reflecting the principle that God does not 'make mistakes' (yaseho). This interpretation aligns with Shia theological emphasis on divine perfection, where 'leaving them' (turk) signifies withholding the reward of those who anticipated the Day of Judgment, while 'leaving in darkness' indicates merciful delay for repentance rather than abandonment.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 1. Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isam al-Kulayni (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Ya`qub alKulayni (RA) said: `Ali ibn Muhammad, famous as `Allan, said: Abu Hamid `Imran ibn Musa ibn Ibrahim on the authority of his brother `Abd al-`Aziz ibn Muslim that I asked Al-Rida `Ali ibn Musa (AS) about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High,
`they hae forsaken Allah, so He has forsaken them.’

So He (AS) said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted be He, neither forgets nor makes mistakes. Indeed, the present creation forgets and makes mistakes. Have you not heard the Mighty and High say: And your Lord is not forgetful. Verily, He punishes the one that forgets Him and forgets the meeting of this Day, and then He makes them to forget themselves. As the Mighty and High says: they forsook Allah, so He made them forsake their own souls: these it is that are the transgressors. And the Word of the Mighty and High: So today We forsake them, as they neglected the meeting of this day of theirs. That is to say “We will abandon them as they neglected to prepare themselves for this Day of Meeting.” The Compiler of this book says: The statement “He will abandon them” means that “He will not reward them” on the Day of Judgement because it is not proper for Allah, the Mighty and High, to abandon. As for the word of Allah the Mighty and High: And left them in utter darkness – they do not see; it means that He will not hasten their punishment, thus granting them time to repent.
